FINDINGS. One measured, non-blocking.
F1 (NON-BLOCKING, MEASURED). The fix adds a per-hook-event cost the module's own docstring says it was designed to avoid. collect_matched_proof_facts's docstring states it reads exactly one file and explicitly rejects "a full parse of every record in proof/ on every hook call (see _MAX_RECORDS's reasoning for why that would not be cheap)". _collect_proven_pr_numbers, added by the fix commit b7343d2, does exactly that: it json.loads every record under proof/ and .lwb/proof/ on every collect_repo_facts call, bounded only by _MAX_RECORDS=5000 files at _MAX_PROOF_RECORD_BYTES=2_000_000 each. Measured, not asserted: on this repository (22 small records) collect_repo_facts costs 2.1 ms/call. On a synthetic consuming repo with 1000 records of 40 KB it costs 111 ms/call with the content scan and 30 ms/call with it stubbed out -- the new scan adds ~81 ms to every hook event at that scale. Non-blocking because (a) the fix is required for correctness, (b) both rules ship at "warn" with nothing armed to deny, (c) the cost is trivial at this repo's size. But collect_matched_proof_facts's stated rationale is now factually stale -- it describes an invariant the module no longer holds -- and a cheaper form exists (parse only records whose filename did not already yield an id, or memoise per repo_root). Recorded for follow-up, not charged against this PR.

NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS.
O1. README's new line "Three rules now enforce something for real, all at warn" -- warn mode reports, it does not enforce. The clause qualifies it immediately, but given this repo's documented history of scoped claims stated broadly, "report" is the honest verb.
O2. _collect_proven_pr_numbers does not skip schema.json / exempt.json the way CI's check_coverage does. Harmless today (neither carries an integer "pr"), but the parity its docstring claims with check_coverage is one exclusion short.
O3. PRE-EXISTING, NOT THIS PR'S: CI's own check_coverage uses `isinstance(data.get("pr"), int)`, which accepts True, and `1 in {True}` is True in Python -- a record with {"pr": true} would mark PR #1 as proven in CI. The adapter added by THIS PR is stricter and correctly excludes bool, so the PR improves on the thing it mirrors. The weakness is in scripts/lwb_check_proof.py on main, and PR #1 is bootstrap-exempt anyway.
O4. "Could not check" and "checked and found nothing" DO share a representation for landed_unproven: M6's exploding collector produced silence indistinguishable from a clean scan, and collect_repo_facts deliberately refuses to set facts_incomplete for it. I am NOT charging this -- the rule never promotes an empty result to "covered", the docstrings say so in three places, and silence is the documented posture. It is, however, fail-OPEN silence, and if lwb_proof_coverage is ever armed to "deny", that is the first shape to revisit.
O5. This branch's proof record is still named proof/lwb-ship-proof-coverage-integrity.json -- #49's branch name, not this one's. It declares {"pr": 50} so CI's coverage check and the new adapter both match it, and lwb_check_proof passes. But collect_matched_proof_facts matches on BRANCH NAME, so on this branch the PR's own record is invisible to its own new lwb_proof_integrity rule (matched_proof_* stay None, rule silent). Not a defect in the code and not a gate failure; worth knowing, because it means this PR does not dogfood that rule on itself.
